title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (char ≠ 2, base S). An elliptic curve E/S determines several objects. J is the étale cubic cover of nonzero 2-torsion points, i.e. the three branch points of E → E/{±1} other than the image of 0. Σ_J is the twisted form of P^1 attached to J, namely E/{±1} with the divisor D_J ≅ J. Σ_J^* = Σ_J − D_J. The section t of Σ_J^* is the image of the zero section, a twisted 'λ-coordinate'. ω_J is presumably the ±1-torsor of 'orientations' of J (square roots of the discriminant of J); this is a guess. The blackboard letter read as 'H' is μ, so μ_4^× is the ±1-torsor of primitive 4th roots of unity.

On the previous page, (30) gives T_{E/S,0}^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}. A 'jacobian rigidification' K is an iso (31) T_{E/S,0} ≅ O(1)_t whose square matches, via (30) and (27), the iso (32). That iso is induced by a section α of μ_2^× ∧ ω_J (33).

This page restates the definition. Giving K is the same as giving a couple (α, K), where:
- α is a section of μ_4^× ∧^{±1} ω_J, i.e. an iso of ±1-torsors μ_4^× ≅ ω_J, a 'partial pinning';
- K is an iso (31) compatible with α.

For fixed α, the K satisfying the square condition form a μ_2-torsor. Grothendieck calls it the torsor of Legendre pinnings ('épinglages de Legendre') of the elliptic curve, associated with the partial pinning α.

Main claim: the fibered category, a stack in groupoids, of elliptic curves with a Legendre pinning is equivalent to the stack of triples (J, t, α):
- (a) J an étale cubic cover of S;
- (b) t a section of Σ_J^*;
- (c) α an iso μ_4^× ≅ ω_J.

The idea of the equivalence: (J, t) gives the P^1-form with four marked points D_J + t, and E is the double cover branched there. That double cover is determined only up to quadratic twist (the μ_2-gerbe, [-1] acting on K by −1). Rigidifying the tangent space at 0 by K kills that ambiguity. α records the compatibility constraint between the square of K and the intrinsic data of J.

A margin NB says the inverse construction of E from (J, t, α) should be made explicit, e.g. via Weierstrass functions. The next page computes automorphisms: the stack is still not rigid. Automorphisms come from automorphisms of J compatible with α and t, which leads to a subscheme P_J of Σ_J^* where t is fixed by an involution ρ.

In modern terms, this is an intrinsic, descent-theoretic (no ordering of 2-torsion) description of the Legendre λ-line moduli problem. It is a twisted-form version of the classical correspondence M_{1,1}[1/2] ↔ M_{0,4}/S_3 together with the μ_2-gerbe.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The claim that the K for fixed α form a μ_2-torsor is correct, since K is determined by its square up to sign.
Small gap: the equivalence (E, K) ↔ (J, t, α) is stated without proof. The inverse construction is explicitly left open in the margin NB.
Notational mismatch with the previous page: there α lives in μ_2^× ∧ ω_J, here in μ_4^× ∧ ω_J. The previous page's machine transcription probably misread μ_4 as μ_2, or the normalization changed.

ideas.what: Intrinsic description of an elliptic curve in char ≠ 2 by (J, t): the étale cubic cover of 2-torsion and a section of the 3-punctured twisted P^1 Σ_J, with E the double cover branched along D_J + t
ideas.modern_name: M_{1,1}[1/2] as a μ_2-gerbe over M_{0,4}/S_3 (λ-line modulo S_3), in twisted form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); in moduli-theoretic form Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Legendre pinning (épinglage de Legendre): a rigidification of the tangent space at 0 by O(1)_t, decomposed into a partial pinning α (iso μ_4^× ≅ ω_J) and a μ_2-torsor of lifts K
ideas.modern_name: Legendre level structure (moduli problem represented by the λ-line)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Mazur, Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves (Legendre family/structure); Igusa

ideas.what: Stack equivalence: elliptic curves with Legendre pinning ≃ triples (J, t, α), with no ordering of 2-torsion points (descent/twisted-forms formulation)
ideas.modern_name: Stack-theoretic description of the Legendre moduli problem via twisted forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore; closest is Katz–Mazur's treatment of the λ-line

missed.claim: The explicit reconstruction of E (with its pinning) from (J, t, α), e.g. via Weierstrass functions, is announced but left undone in the margin.
missed.quote: NB Il faudrait expliciter la construction de (E, ...) en termes des données (J, t, α) ... (via fonctions ℘ de Weierstrass etc.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The construction is standard in coordinates (Legendre form y² = x(x−1)(x−λ)). A clean coordinate-free version over a general base, with J non-split, is a pleasant but routine exercise.

missed.claim: A twisted-form (non-split J), coordinate-free formulation of the Legendre moduli problem. The fourth-roots-of-unity torsor μ_4^× is identified with the orientation torsor ω_J, explaining intrinsically the role of √−1 in Legendre normalization. This intrinsic packaging is not standard in the literature, though the content is known.
missed.quote: α sections de μ^×_4 ∧ ω_J, i.e. iso. μ^×_4 ≃ ω_J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of expository and historical interest. It shows Grothendieck treating M_{1,1}[1/2] versus M_{0,4} (central to his Esquisse/Teichmüller-tower program) at the level of stacks and gerbes in the early 1980s.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially classical material: the Legendre λ-line and the M_{1,1}/M_{0,4} relation, recast intrinsically via torsors and twisted forms. The μ_4^× ≅ ω_J formulation is a nice touch, but its content is known.
